Question: If someone gives me a gift, is it my possession? Can I sell it? My nephew made me some ugly clay thing in his second grade art class and I wish to sell it for some weed.
Answer: Of course it’s yours. And you can sell it, break it, throw it away, if you want. No one really cares what you do with it.

Question: As a landlord, should I advise the tenant to move out before the eviction hearing in court?
Answer: No. A tenant could then use that against you. “He told me I HAD to move out even though he hadn’t filed anything…” That can come back to bite you. Your jurisdiction will have specific notices that must be served to the tenant - “cure or quit”, “unlawful detainer”, etc. The contents of those notices are ALL that the tenant should be told about what to do.

Question: Is it concerning that an ex and the new relationship have been caught videotaping me in my own home without any knowledge or permission, has this happened to you and what happened? And should I be concerned for safety of myself and guests?
Answer: If you didn’t know about it, how do you know it was happening? How’d they get INTO your home to videotape you? Surely you changed the locks after your ex left!

Question: My boyfriend is breaking up with me after one year because of my parents being against the relationship even though they are fine with it now, he says it will give him too much stress. Should I try convincing him?
Answer: No, you should not. He wants out of the relationship. Your parents are merely the excuse he’s using. So let him go. Why would you want to “convince” someone to be with you when he clearly doesn't WANT to be with you?

Question: Is it normal for a wife not to save the contact number of her husband?
Answer: There’s nothing wrong with not saving it. It’s not like she needs to look him up - surely she KNOWS his number.
